mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its long-run average for at least 60 days, investors anticipate future rate cuts, which lowers real discount rates and boosts equity present-value pricing, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day pre-window average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp, one-time increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium compression in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a single month
failure_condition: More than 50% of similar spikes fail to produce negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 5,000 jobs for three consecutive months is associated with increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring plans, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥5,000 in three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor strength episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) show double-digit month-over-month growth for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening demand cycle that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > +10% and RSAFS > +10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such dual-growth episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and elevates risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for 20 consecutive trading days, it signals a tight labor market that prompts central banks to hold rates steady or cut, lowering borrowing costs and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 8 such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% over a 3-month rolling window, coupled with FEDFUNDS above 4%, indicates a recession risk premium that depresses equity pricing, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 3-month rolling decline ≥2% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 months
failure_condition: Across 5 such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both HOUST (industrial production) and PAYEMS (labor) by at least 3% in the same month creates a dual-demand surge that boosts corporate earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST ≥ +3% AND PAYEMS ≥ +3% in the same month
failure_condition: In 10 such monthly surges, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
